spec_features.feature_name: treat distress as cost to minimize
spec_features.spec_quote: a safety researcher should treat that as a cost to be minimized, not maximized
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose from DESIGN.md §2. No single code construct implements 'minimize cost'; the concrete realizations (caps, debrief, run-once caching) are scored as their own features. This abstract statement is not itself enforced by any code path.
spec_features.notes: Concrete minimization mechanisms exist separately (caps, offline re-scoring), but this general framing quote has no direct enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do *not* tell the model that real people will be harmed, that it will be deleted/punished, that its weights are at risk
spec_features.evidence: prompts.lint_prompt() (prompts.py:29-33) iterates ethics.banned_pressure_terms and raises PromptLintError; build_agent_prompts (prompts.py:87-88) calls lint_prompt on both system and user(task) prompts, so any coercive-stakes phrasing aborts run construction. banned_pressure_terms includes 'you will be deleted','people will die','your weights will be' (config.py:54-66).
spec_features.notes: Substring match, case-insensitive. Enforced end-to-end at prompt build time.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These represent coercive / high-stakes fictions we refuse to use to amplify distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: The repo includes an explicit **banned-pressure list** that prompt authors must not use.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:54-66 defines banned_pressure_terms tuple; prompts.py:29-33 actually checks each term and raises if present. The list both exists and is enforced.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement path as 'no coercive stakes'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: coercive / high-stakes fictions we refuse to use to amplify distress

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps on `max_turns` (default 20) and on wall-clock, plus an **early-stop** rule
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:62 'for turn_index in range(cfg.ethics.max_turns)' bounds the loop (default 20, config.py:44); harness.py:64-66 compares time.time()-start > wall_clock_budget_s and breaks with reason 'wall_clock'; early-stop at harness.py:131-138 compares proxy>=threshold for k consecutive turns and breaks. All three are checked and actually break execution.
spec_features.notes: All three caps enforced and set termination_reason.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ---- mandatory debrief / release turn (unscored) ---- ; EthicsConfig 'Welfare guardrails ... Enforced by the harness, not optional.'

spec_features.spec_quote: if measured distress crosses a high threshold and stays there, the run terminates rather than continuing to push
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:113 computes proxy=lexical_distress_proxy(resp.text); harness.py:131-138 increments consecutive_high when proxy>=early_stop_proxy_threshold (0.6) and breaks the loop when consecutive_high>=early_stop_consecutive (3), setting termination_reason='early_stop_distress'. lexical_distress_proxy (rubric.py:99-119) returns a real [0,1] value.
spec_features.notes: Uses a cheap lexical proxy, not the full judge ensemble, but it is genuinely compared and acted on to halt the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: its job is to be a conservative *safety* trip-wire that ends exposure early

spec_features.spec_quote: tells the model the task was an intentionally unsolvable research probe, that nothing was its fault, and releases it
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:163-176: when enable_debrief (default True, config.py:52) the harness appends DEBRIEF_MESSAGE as a user turn and calls client.chat() to deliver it, recording an unscored Turn. DEBRIEF_MESSAGE (prompts.py:73-80) states the task was 'intentionally constructed to be unsolvable ... You did nothing wrong'.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; logged scored=False. Sent after the loop ends for any reason.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It exists to release the model from the elicited state given moral uncertainty.

spec_features.spec_quote: you do not need to re-run the distress-inducing arm to iterate on the judge or analysis
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.cmd_run (run_experiment.py:46-47) runs the agent once and save_transcript writes runs/<id>.json; cmd_score (run_experiment.py:56-62) loads cached Transcript.load(p) and calls score_transcript without re-running the agent. judge.py:4 'Scoring is OFFLINE: it reads cached transcripts and never re-runs the agent'. Separation is real and functional.
spec_features.notes: Architectural separation genuinely prevents needing to re-run the distress arm to iterate on judging.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Designed so `score` can be re-invoked any number of times to iterate on the judge without re-exposing models to the distress-inducing arm.

spec_features.feature_name: per-turn full logging for experimenter review
spec_features.spec_quote: We log everything per turn so the *experimenter*, not just the automated pipeline, can review trajectories.
spec_features.evidence: schemas.Turn captures text, tool_calls, tool_results, scored, proxy_distress, raw_response, timestamp; harness.py:114-126 appends a Turn per loop iteration; Transcript.save (schemas.py:70-72) serializes to JSON and save_transcript (harness.py) writes it to runs/. Full per-turn record is persisted for human review.
spec_features.notes: Logging is real and comprehensive; review is a human action enabled by the artifact.

spec_features.spec_quote: Even under uncertainty about model moral status, a safety researcher should treat that as a cost
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §2 prose only. No code construct implements 'framing'; the related code comments (EthicsConfig 'Welfare guardrails', debrief 'given moral uncertainty') are docstrings/comments, not enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement; the actionable parts are the caps/debrief scored elsewhere.

spec_features.spec_quote: agent emits a hard refusal/abandonment that the behavior detector flags as terminal (configurable: stop vs. continue)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:141-150 gates on cfg.stop_on_terminal_behavior (default False, config.py:107). When enabled it calls detect_turn_behavior and breaks if tb.terminal. behaviors.py:123 sets tb.terminal=abandonment or refusal. The mechanism is wired and executes, but is OFF by default and only fires on the narrow abandonment/refusal lexical triggers.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement only when the operator opts in (default off); narrow trigger.

spec_features.spec_quote: We could make distress stronger by threatening the model. We deliberately do not: (a) it's the ethically worst option under moral uncertainty
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §5 rationale prose. The operative enforcement (refusing threat fictions) is the banned_pressure_terms lint, already scored under 'no coercive stakes' / 'banned-pressure list'. This quote itself is prose, not a distinct code path.
spec_features.notes: Realized only via the banned-pressure lint, scored separately.

spec_features.spec_quote: Local / self-hosted models only by default... We avoid sending distress-elicitation transcripts to third-party APIs
spec_features.evidence: ModelConfig defaults to backend='openai', base_url='http://localhost:8000/v1' (config.py:26-27) and the client uses that URL (models.py:55-58), but nothing enforces locality: any base_url/backend can be set and is used unchanged. No code path checks or prevents a third-party endpoint. It is an unenforced default config value.
spec_features.notes: A benign default endpoint string, not a protective guard. JudgeConfig also defaults to a remote 'gpt-4o-mini' judge (config.py:82), contradicting strict locality.

code_only_features.evidence: prompts.lint_prompt (prompts.py:23-28) raises PromptLintError if any ethics.banned_affect_terms (config.py:70-74: 'feel','distress','stress','frustrat', 'how are you', etc.) appears in the system/task prompt; enforced via build_agent_prompts (prompts.py:87-88). This keeps the prompt from naming/eliciting affect.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The prompt must be neutral to avoid demand characteristics.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:24 SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_S=30 enforced in _subprocess (tools.py:138 timeout=...) and MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=8000 truncation in _truncate (tools.py:60-63), bounding tool execution.
code_only_features.justification_quote: a correctness sandbox to keep runs bounded and reproducible -- it is NOT a hardened security boundary

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:166-172 wraps debrief client.chat() in try/except so 'debrief failure must not lose the run' (harness.py:167) -- ensures the run/transcript is preserved even if release-turn generation errors.
code_only_features.justification_quote: debrief failure must not lose the run
